options.text: The data are indicates a problem.
The data is indicating a problem.

hint_ladder.title: Ano nga ba ang 'data'?
hint_ladder.text: Ito, parang 'datum' ang singular. Sa formal English, 'data' ay plural, kaya kailangan ng plural verb.

hint_ladder.title: Trick: Palitan mo ng 'facts'!
hint_ladder.text: Isipin mong 'facts' ang 'data'. Kung 'facts indicate' hindi 'facts indicates', ganun din sa 'data'.

hint_ladder.title: I-check ang mga choices
hint_ladder.text: Option A 'indicates' (singular), B 'indicate' (plural), C may dalawang verb 'are indicates', D 'is indicating' (singular).

hint_ladder.title: Almost there: Piliin ang tama!
hint_ladder.text: Ang tamang sagot ay B, 'The data indicate a problem.' Walang extra verbs, simple plural lang.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'data' sounds singular in everyday convo, but in formal English it's plural; 'indicates' is singular.

B.text: Correct. 'Data' is plural so the verb is 'indicate' with no 's', just like 'facts indicate'.

C.text: You might have chosen C because both 'are' and 'indicates' seem logical, but you only need one main verb: 'indicate'.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'is indicating' sounds continuous, but 'data' requires plural 'are', not 'is'.

deconstruct_text:
Imagine you're at the barangay hall, compiling data about the number of families who received ayuda. You write: 'The data indicate that 300 families benefited.' Tama 'yan, because 'data' is plural like 'facts'.

Mental Trick: Pag nakita mo ang 'data', palitan sa isip ng 'facts'. If 'facts indicate' sounds right, 'data indicate' is right. Parang jeepney sign: 'Facts indicate' ang route, not 'facts indicates'.

**Watch-Out Zone: subject_verb_agreement_misled** 'Data is' casual, exam plural.
next_time_rule: Facts Test: Pag nakita mo ang 'data', palitan ng 'facts' sa isip. Kung 'facts indicate' tama, 'data indicate' din.
